chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about a woman who heard that a man had divorced her, and he denied it. Should she stay with him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, for his divorce without witnesses is not a divorce, and the divorce to other than the waiting period is not a divorce, and it is not permissible for him to do so by divorcing her without witnesses and to other than the waiting period which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband denies it and there are no witnesses?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that a woman may remain with her husband if he claims to have divorced her but she only heard it, as his unilateral declaration without witnesses or adherence to the prescribed waiting period (iddah) is not a valid divorce. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on procedural integrity in divorce, ensuring that a man cannot unilaterally sever the marital bond without fulfilling the conditions commanded by Allah. The hadith highlights the principle that 'talq bi-ghayr shuhud' (divorce without witnesses) is legally ineffective, protecting the wife from arbitrary dismissal.
